solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Was quoted as being exuberant

parts.note: ex- means former, what was once
to cite is to quote, so quoted gives cited

explanation.surface: Someone reported to have been in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Was quoted' as EX (former) plus CITED (quoted), joined into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant and excited are near synonyms for being full of eager energy.

clue.text: Executive committee blocks copy

parts.note: EC is the abbreviation for executive committee
printing type is made of metal blocks

explanation.surface: A company's board stops something being duplicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Blocks looks like a verb, but it is the printer's metal pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectype is a reproduction, as opposed to the original prototype.

clue.text: Hundred going right way for assembly

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
on course means heading in the right direction

explanation.surface: A hundred people heading the correct way to a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a crowd or gathering of people, as well as the open hall where they gather.

clue.text: One wrote about lookalike article included

indicators.note: the double goes around the article
the article is taken in among the letters of the other word

parts.note: a twin is someone who looks just like another
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An author wrote about a double, with a piece in a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A sits inside TWIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American author Samuel Clemens, a writer.

clue.text: Cover vehicle taking turn with goods

parts.note: a deck covers a ship's hull
a car is a vehicle
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Insuring a car while delivering merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck cargo is freight carried on a ship's open deck rather than in the hold.

clue.text: Lady embraced a new queen in Europe

indicators.note: the lady's name holds the next two letters inside it, as in a hug

parts.note: Julia is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman hugged a newly crowned European monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: AN goes inside JULIA, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliana was Queen of the Netherlands from 1948 to 1980, a European monarch.

clue.text: Thanks lady shortly before council

indicators.note: the shortened name comes first in the answer
cut short, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Juno, queen of the Roman gods, is the lady here
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Thanking a woman briefly before a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Juno is the Roman queen of the gods; drop her last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a ruling group or council, especially one seizing power after a coup.

clue.text: Matthew is cut out of book

parts.note: the apostle Matthew was also called Levi

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A gospel writer gets removed from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew was also called Levi in the Gospels; IS CUT rearranges to TICUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviticus is the third book of the Old Testament, setting out priestly law.

clue.text: Sailor on edge completely full

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A seaman at the brink, utterly sated.
explanation.definitionFit: Brimming to the top: abrim describes a vessel filled right up.

clue.text: Many-sided despite having no sides

definitions.meaning: first meaning: versatile, skilled in every aspect
second meaning: round all over, like a ball, so without flat faces

explanation.walkthrough: The contradiction is the joke: a versatile person is many-sided, and a perfect sphere has no sides at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is versatile, while a shape that is round everywhere has no edges or flat faces.

clue.text: Vehicle located in Kensington Gardens

indicators.note: the answer is found sitting inside the next two words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A car parked in a famous London park.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of KensingTON GArdens.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India, so a kind of conveyance.

clue.text: May state a learner is found at cape

parts.note: may, meaning is able or permitted, gives can
to aver is to state firmly
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A learner driver might be found at a coastal headland.
explanation.walkthrough: May is the verb here, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral is the Florida headland famous for space launches.

clue.text: Another ocean ship leaving south about one for ancient land

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the next piece, so about signals one thing surrounding another
another form of the words means their letters are made into a different arrangement
the south letter departs from the two words, so it is removed

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A second sea-going vessel departs southward for an old country.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from OCEAN SHIP to leave OCEANHIP, rearrange it ('Another') and wrap it 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was the ancient seafaring civilisation on the coast of what is now Lebanon.

clue.text: Time in bars

parts.note: bars are musical measures, not pubs or prisons, and the time of the music is its speed

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests time spent in pubs or in prison; the bars are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed at which a piece of music is played, measured across its bars.

clue.text: Not one vulgar part

parts.note: proper means decent, the opposite of vulgar
a fraction is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: A claim that no section of something is crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Vulgar is also the maths term for a common fraction, and the proper kind is less than one, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, a fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator, worth less than one whole.

clue.text: Favourite going over less than half Mongolian capital with this French impatience

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece goes over, above, the rest

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
Ulan Bator is the capital of Mongolia; its first four of nine letters are less than half of it
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A darling travels across part of Asia's steppe with this French irritability.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulan Bator is Mongolia's capital; keep its first four letters, fewer than half of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish bad temper, a peevish impatience with others.

clue.text: Jack's drink messenger took from contrabandist

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and rum is the traditional naval drink
a runner carries messages

explanation.surface: A sailor's tipple taken by a courier from a smuggler.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-runner smuggled liquor, especially during Prohibition, so was a smuggler of contraband.

clue.text: Cooler alcoholic receptacle perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that chills, here a pail of ice for bottles
second meaning: a container one might keep wine or champagne in at table

explanation.walkthrough: Cooler reads like a comparison or a prison, but it is the chilling vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the pail of ice used to chill bottles of wine or champagne at table.

clue.text: Journalist following game was made to seem small

indicators.note: the journalist comes after the game in the answer

parts.note: squash is a racket game
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter arriving after a match feels belittled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be squashed is to be crushed or humiliated, cut down to size.

clue.text: Equestrian most puzzled by president

indicators.note: being puzzled means mixed up, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rider is baffled by the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: President here is the person presiding over a quiz, not a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: The quizmaster presides over a quiz, putting the questions to contestants, so chairs it.

clue.text: Thin outer layer only at intervals

parts.note: skin is the outer layer of the body

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word, the even ones

explanation.surface: Slim, with only a patchy outer covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very lean or slender, with little flesh.

clue.text: One part of wedding dress said to be of value

indicators.note: said signals that the words are heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one; a bride's veil is part of her outfit

explanation.surface: Something about a bridal outfit is said to be valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: A VEIL, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or benefit, as in 'to no avail'.

clue.text: Arizona detective an old Mexican

parts.note: AZ is the postal code for Arizona
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A detective from Arizona and an old man from Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people of the empire in central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Friar went round stormy lough having expression of sympathy

indicators.note: the friar's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion

indicators.note: a stormy lake is churned up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monk walked around a rough Irish lake while consoling someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A lough is an Irish lake, and Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion; 'stormy' churns the lake's letters before the friar goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Said to someone after a misfortune, the phrase offers commiseration, though often wryly.

clue.text: Endless anger, Edward going round exhausted

indicators.note: the name surrounds the shortened word

parts.note: Ted is a pet form of Edward

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Edward, worn out, circles in an unending rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted is the usual short form of Edward; 'Endless' trims the anger before he goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired and exhausted are synonyms for being drained of energy.

clue.text: Possess about 50 cut in two equal parts

indicators.note: the verb wraps around the numeral

parts.note: to have is to possess
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Owning around fifty things and splitting them evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to divide it into two matching halves.

clue.text: Accident in turn had potential!

indicators.note: potential suggests a possible other form, so these letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: An accident that, at its moment, might have happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters have the potential to become something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A road collision where the driver leaves without stopping is a classic kind of accident.

clue.text: Be pleased with name for match

parts.note: to like something is to be pleased with it

explanation.surface: Happy with the title chosen for a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Match is a verb here, as in compare, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare or match them up.

clue.text: Last month rush to get appointed

parts.note: December is the final month, abbreviated DEC
a rush is a reed-like plant of wet places

explanation.surface: A hurry at the end of the year to be given a post.
explanation.walkthrough: Rush is the waterside plant, not a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decreed is ordained or fixed by authority, as an appointed date is.

clue.text: Disheartened never to return and attempt coming in again

indicators.note: returning means the shortened word is read backwards
losing its heart means the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A dispirited person vows never to go back, then tries anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes the middle letter of never, V, and 'to return' reads what is left backwards before the attempt follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry is the act of entering again, as a spacecraft does into the atmosphere.
